D.t: Gina Hinojosa trails by 2.3 and wins 30% of simulations. Closing it takes about 115,973 voters switching sides, or 231,945 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +8.1 and D +3.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +3.3. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at D +2.3; your worst is Marist University at R +6.1. 24 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Travis, a projected net 304,638 votes; Dallas, a projected net 281,431 votes; Harris, a projected net 274,411 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +7.1, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +0.7, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, R +2.2, 3.8% of the vote; Williamson, D +11.2, 2.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Gina Hinojosa runs furthest behind in Lubbock, Montgomery, Bell. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 57 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 54 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.10 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 37 to 62, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.03 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Gina Hinojosa: Immigration voters 18 to 80, Small counties 22 to 76, Midsize counties 33 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$4.0M cash against $18.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Cash: $18.2M in the bank against $4.0M for Gina Hinojosa.

R.t: Greg Abbott leads by 2.3 in the forecast and wins 70% of simulations. The cushion is about 231,945 votes; a one point swing is about 49,988 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +3.6 and R +8.1. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +3.3. Your best recent poll is Marist University at R +6.1; your worst is New York Times/Siena at D +2.3. 24 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Montgomery, a projected net 100,218 votes; Parker, a projected net 45,528 votes; Smith, a projected net 37,417 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tarrant, D +7.1, 7.2% of the vote; Collin, D +0.7, 4.4% of the vote; Denton, R +2.2, 3.8% of the vote; Williamson, D +11.2, 2.7% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Greg Abbott runs furthest behind in Hidalgo, Travis, Hays. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 68% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 44 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.10 points; White voters, 61% of voters, 62 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.03 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Greg Abbott: Black voters 20 to 78, Independents 27 to 70, Moderates 36 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18.2M cash against $4.0M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

media.what: His 2WAY 'Midterm Blitz' coverage described both the Texas governor and Senate races as in play, citing Vance's return to the state and money flowing to Paxton.
Interviewed Democratic nominee Gina Hinojosa about what it would take to unseat Gov. Greg Abbott.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Abbott vs Hinojosa from Likely R to Lean R.
Inside Elections moved the Texas governor race between Greg Abbott and Gina Hinojosa from Likely Republican to Lean Republican.
